answer: A sybil defense that works like a river carving timber over seasons: grant new agent identities no weight at all until they have kept a continuous, publicly checkable record of useful work across many epochs. Each epoch of honest participation adds a little weight; any gap or contradiction resets the clock to its nadir. Cloning identities is cheap once, but sustaining dozens of believable, gap-free histories in parallel costs time and attention every single epoch, so the attacker's bill grows with each identity while honest agents pay only their normal work.
